In addition to them, all the people became frightened. They did not know the essence of these products, and
they were thinking that the universe was about to be destroyed. Meaning: According to the seventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita, the laws of nature are so strict that
no living being can transgress them. It has also been said that in devotion to Krishna,
only the soul completely dedicated to Krishna can be saved. From this description of Srimad Bhagavat, we can
know that the birth of two great demons led to numerous natural disasters starting to occur.
Indirectly, it should be understood that as has been described before, when
such disasters continuously occur on Earth, it indicates that some demonic people
have been born, or their number has increased. In ancient times, even though there were only two demons born from Diti, so much destruction occurred. Nowadays, especially in this Kali Yuga, such
mischiefs are seen regularly, which indicate that there has been a definite increase in the demonic population.
To prevent the increase in demonic population, in the Vedic civilization, there were many rules of social life,
of which, to get good children, the Garbhadhana Sanskar is the main one)
In the Bhagavad Gita, Arjuna says to Sri Krishna that if inter-caste people are born, then this whole
world will look like hell. People desire peace in the world, but due to not being able to take advantage of the Garbhadhana Sanskar, many unwanted children keep being born, just as demons were born from Diti's womb. Diti was so lustful that she forced her husband to have intercourse in an inauspicious time, due to which the demons who created chaos were born. A human being
should follow the rules while having intercourse to produce offspring, so that there is good
offspring. If every family follows the Vedic method, then good children will be born,
there will be no demons, and peace will be established in the world. If we do not follow the rules of social peace in our lives,
we should not expect peace.
